name: YJ-18 anti-ship cruise missile
overview_md:
The YJ-18 is the PLA Navy's primary surface-fleet and submarine anti-ship cruise missile, and the weapon that gives China's modern destroyers their offensive bite. Conceptually similar to Russia's Kalibr/Klub family, it combines the two virtues that usually trade off against each other: long range and a high-speed terminal attack.

The missile cruises subsonically for most of its flight to maximise range — assessed at roughly 290 km and possibly more — then, in the final tens of kilometres, a separating supersonic sprint stage accelerates to around Mach 2.5–3 for the terminal run-in, drastically cutting the defender's reaction time. Launched from the Mk-41-equivalent universal vertical launch systems on Type 052D and Type 055 destroyers (and in encapsulated form from submarines), it lets a single Chinese surface action group threaten opposing ships from well beyond their own anti-ship reach.

For an analyst, the YJ-18 is the reason the PLA Navy's surface combatants are credible blue-water threats rather than coastal defenders. It out-ranges the legacy U.S. Harpoon and competes with newer Western weapons, and its VLS basing means a Type 055 can carry a large mixed magazine of anti-ship, land-attack and air-defence rounds — a flexibility that mirrors the U.S. Navy's own move toward multi-mission VLS loadouts.

additional.flight_profile: Sea-skimming subsonic cruise, supersonic terminal stage

builder: China Aerospace Science and Industry Corp. (CASIC)

combat_history.event: No combat use; routinely exercised by PLAN surface and submarine forces.
combat_history.significance: Capability assessed from deployments and exercises.

modernization.description: Integrated into the universal VLS of Type 052D and Type 055 for mixed anti-ship/land-attack/air-defence loadouts.
modernization.impact: Gives PLAN surface groups flexible, deep offensive magazines.

vulnerabilities.description: Long-range shots need over-the-horizon targeting data.
vulnerabilities.context: Defender EW and decoys can disrupt the terminal seeker.

vulnerabilities.description: The supersonic sprint is short but detectable once it separates.
vulnerabilities.context: Fast networked CIWS/SAMs can still engage.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Fleet anti-ship engagements from destroyer VLS and submarine tubes beyond the enemy's anti-ship range.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Type 055/052D surface action groups; Type 093 submarines.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Standard fit on modern PLAN combatants.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Both pair subsonic cruise with a supersonic terminal sprint stage; the YJ-18 is China's equivalent.
Harpoon is subsonic and shorter-ranged; the YJ-18 substantially out-ranges it.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Why the US Navy is racing past Harpoon.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: YJ-12 is supersonic throughout but shorter-ranged; YJ-18 cruises subsonic for reach.

doctrine.role: Fleet anti-ship cruise missile giving PLAN surface ships and submarines long-range offensive reach.
doctrine.employment: Subsonic cruise for range, supersonic terminal sprint to defeat point defences; fired from universal VLS.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Range and terminal speed together — the Kalibr concept, navalised for China.
doctrine.threat_context: Makes modern PLAN combatants credible blue-water surface threats.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against Russia's Kalibr, the U.S. Harpoon and China's own YJ-12.
